discussion_comments.comment_body: Since this wasn't on in OSS, we should enable it first before removal

@eps1lon Can you explain why is it required? I am not sure I understand the reason for it.

Do you want to keep the flag present, but enable it everywhere?
Enable it everywhere first. This is how we do rollouts for all feature flags. This ensures we can easily disable the feature if it breaks something in OSS.
@eps1lon Thanks, got it! Published https://github.com/react/react/pull/37039 to proceed.
We use gate('flag') for this instead of importing the feature flag module.

No reason to leave it off in React Native, testing etc. since there's no renderer being used anyway but it ensures that we don't get blocked trying to remove the flag later and people don't know if it's safe to remove.
This block isn't gated on `enableAsyncDebugInfo` but `resolveDebugValue` is only callable with `enableAsyncDebugInfo`. `enableAsyncDebugInfo` isn't enabled everywhere at the moment.
I guess this is implied via `payload._ioInfo` but still nice for DCE and readability to gate it.
Fixed. The whole block should've been gated before just like the reject.

It would be a breaking change but my preference would be that this is only on for `DEV` and not if `isDevToolsPresent`. Since otherwise if I have a profiling build and I have devtools installed, but my colleague doesn't, it can be confusing why it doesn't work. Whereas if it's always `<Profiler>` that opt-in to profiling builds then I'd have to add it and then my colleague would see it too.
